summary: Pend Oreille County, WA: a 15-foot pole L-4 lookout built in 1934 on the Kaniksu National Forest, removed or destroyed in the 1960s; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 15' pole tower with L-4 cab; a 60' pole tower 1/4 mile to the northeast was also part of the site
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in the 1960s; no source describes what, if anything, remains

events.note: 15-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; a 60-foot pole tower 1/4 mile northeast was also part of the site
Only the decade is given (the 1960s). Sources differ: removed (firetower.org), destroyed (firelookout.com), removed or destroyed (WillhiteWeb). Forest Lookouts lists only Removed with no date.
Registered December 14, 2012 as US 1498, WA 398; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources agree on the 1960s but differ on the word: removed (firetower.org), destroyed (firelookout.com), removed or destroyed (WillhiteWeb). Forest Lookouts gives only Removed. The story reports the decade and the difference in wording.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked and correct (status gone, 2012 registration, elevation 5,416 ft). The brief had no 'built' event; 1934 added from all four sources. Four of the five sources are hobby or register sites that share one underlying record; no Forest Service or NRHP primary record was checked, so the 1960s end date rests on those sites. The 1939 Gleason Mountain Fire is a different event: the federal Lessons Learned page (lessons.wildfire.gov) lists it in Idaho on the Kaniksu NF and no source ties it to this lookout, so it is left out of the story. No staffing records found. No source describes the site today or public access. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 5 page reads.
